div.head: I Cn 17.1
div.ab: And sancte Eadweardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eall Englaland (þæt is on þam feowerteoðan dæge on Martige, XVIIII.) kl. Aprilis ⁊ sancte Dunstanes mæssedæg on XIIII. kl. Iunii (þæt ys on þam þreotteoðan dæge þe byð on Mæge).
⁊ sancte Eadwardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eall Englaland on quintadecima kalendas Aprilis ⁊ sancte Dunstanes mæssedæg on XIIII. kl. Iunii.
Ænd sancte Eadwærdes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoron, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eall Englaland on XV. kl. Apr. and sancte Dunstanes mæssedæg on XIIII. kl. Iunii.
Et sancti regis Eadwardi gloriosum passionis diem per totam Angliam uolumus celebrari XV. kl. Aprilis et sancti Dunstani XIIII. kl. Iunii.
[17, 1] Sapientes regni mei mecum decreuerunt celebrari festiuitatem sancti Eadƿardi regis XV. kl. Aprilis et sancti Dunstani XIIII. kl. Iunii.
Et festum sancti Edwardi sapientes instituerunt seruari per totam Angliam XV. kalendas Aprilis, necnon et sancti Dunstani XIIII. kal. Iunii.
⁊ sancte Eadwardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eall Englaland on quintadecima kalendas Aprilis ⁊ sancte Dunstanes mæssedæg on XIIII kl. Iunii.

And Sancte Eadweardes mæssedæg witan habbað gecoren, þæt man freolsian sceal ofer eall Englaland, þæt is on þam XV dæge (on Martige XVIII) kalendas Aprilis and Sancte Dunstanes mæssedæg on XIIII kalendas Iunii, þæt ys on þam þreotteoðan dæge þe byð on Mæge.

Und des heiligen Eadward Fest haben die Witan entschieden, dass man über ganz England feiern soll am 18. März (nämlich am 14. irrig G) und des heiligen Dunstan Festtag am 19. Mai (d. h. am 13. Mai irrig G).

And the witan have chosen that the feast of St Edward is to be celebrated throughout all England on 18 March (namely on the 14th, wrongly, G), and the feast of St Dunstan on 19 May (that is, on 13 May, wrongly, G).
And the authorities have decided that St Edward's festival shall be celebrated throughout England on the 18th of March, and St Dunstan's festival on the 19th of May.

And the council has determined that the Feast of Saint Edward shall be celebrated throughout England on the fifteenth day before the kalends of April (the nineteenth of March) and the Feast of Saint Dunstan on the fourteenth day before the kalends of June, that is, the thirteenth day of May.

div.note: G's two bracketed glosses (‘þæt is … XVIIII.’ and ‘þæt ys … on Mæge’) are only in G and wrong; Liebermann corrects to ‘on XV. kl.’ from the other MSS and VI Atr. G's ‘XVIIII’ was altered to ‘XV’. Liebermann compares VI Atr 23.1.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 299, October 2026 (MS Cons); AU: corrected against Rabin p. 246 / 247, October 2026 (was “xiiii”, now “XIIII”); AY: corrected against Rabin p. 246 / 247, October 2026 (was “xviiii: xviii”, now “XVIIII: XVIII”); AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 246 / 247, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “|”)
nineteenth day of March: The scribe errs here, writing the eighteenth of March rather than the nineteenth.

‘glorios’ nennt Q Eadwards II. Todestag nur nach der Phrase der Märtyrerlegende: der Ermordete starb nicht für eine Idee.—Inst und Cons nennen den Heiligen nicht Märtyrer, unterscheiden ihn also nicht vom Bekenner († 1066). Sie schreiben daher, bevor dieser 1163 heilig gesprochen ward, und wahrscheinlich sogar bevor er um 1150 heilig hiess

Q calls the day of Eadward II’s death ‘glorious’ merely following the phrasing of the martyr legend: the murdered king did not die for an idea.—Inst and Cons do not call the saint a martyr, and so do not distinguish him from the Confessor († 1066). They therefore write before the latter was canonized in 1163, and probably even before he was called a saint, c. 1150
Kein blosser Schreibfehler in G, da 14. März = 19 kl. Apr.
Not a mere slip of the pen in G, since 14 March = 19 kl. Apr.
